title: Week Summary: Evolution, Governance, and Architecture Debt

concepts.name: Evolution perspective
concepts.description: A perspective focused on how the architecture supports planned and unplanned change over time.

concepts.name: Change driver
concepts.description: A business, technical, regulatory, operational, or user force that may require architecture change.

concepts.name: Volatility point
concepts.description: A part of the system expected to change more often than surrounding elements.

concepts.name: Extension point
concepts.description: A designed place where new behavior or variation can be added with limited disruption.

concepts.name: Architecture governance
concepts.description: Practices that guide, review, and sustain architectural decisions across delivery work.

concepts.name: Architecture guardrail
concepts.description: A rule, standard, automated check, or review boundary that helps teams make safe local decisions.

concepts.name: Decision authority
concepts.description: The person, team, or forum responsible for approving or owning an architectural decision.

concepts.name: Governance feedback loop
concepts.description: A mechanism that uses delivery experience, incidents, metrics, and reviews to adjust architectural guidance.

concepts.name: Architecture debt
concepts.description: A structural or decision-related weakness that increases future cost, risk, delay, or fragility.

concepts.name: Architecture refactoring
concepts.description: A deliberate change to improve architectural structure without primarily adding user-visible features.

concepts.name: Debt evidence
concepts.description: Observed delay, defect, incident, complexity, or cost that demonstrates architectural debt impact.

concepts.name: Migration path
concepts.description: A planned sequence of changes that moves the system from current architecture to a target architecture.
